question: Can a public-pair-dependent rational curve force a rational relation on every reduced inverse-pair event, and what public test identifies that event?
fields: all eight selected fields in input order
generator: m times reduction of rational P=(2,2), where m=ord(P mod p)/q
target: Q=17G; fixture scalar used for replay after any relation
query_law: complete lexicographic ordered (t1,t2) in [0,q)^2; R_i=Q-t_i G
admission: both reduced points nonidentity and distinct
public_test: one reduced-group addition R1+R2 per admissible query
adaptive_curve: on a public inverse-pair hit, center x,y of R1; take E_Q: Y^2=X^3-X+B with B=y^2-x^3+x; lift R1=(x,y), R2=(x,-y)
curve_construction: one integer B and exact nonsingularity and reduction check per reduced hit
raw_rows: deterministic gzip JSONL shards by field and blocks of 32 t1 values; every query status retained
claim_boundary: adaptive rational relation construction on the already-public inverse-pair event; no generic success, wall-time, or IC speedup claim
